He had become the chosen one of a god, and now he had control of thousands of eldritch horrors - and more were being created every time he bade them overrun another font of power. These things, they fed off it like so many ants stripping the bones of a Med’ja clean. Already twelve things Tymoro called “Gibbering Orbs” had arisen and started assuming responsibilities for the control of the Gibberings. The Coin still held control over them, but the swarm as a whole started getting… smarter. The next natural spring was up ahead, gushing power like a waterspout, overflowing and spurting out. Like the first time and every other time had had come to a place of this power, his hair stood on end.

This specific place of power was a literal springs. The water ran clean and pure with more than a touch of magic. Pausing, he dumped out his waterskins and refilled them from the springs. The water was cold and clear, he had come to know that this unnatural coldness in things meant there was magic afoot. The water in the spring shimmered and shook and Yeron’s reflection was replaced with that of a disembodied bronze mask. In that moment, he saw what he truly was, and he looked *good*. “Hello, Tymoro.” Yeron said, “What brings you here today?” Tymoro rippled with the movements of the water. His voice came through, however, strong and brassy, like the blowing of a thousand horns, each one at a different pitch. [M] CAPSLOCK [/M] “I have a blessing for you. One of my own. As you know, your people bring misfortune to all that gaze upon you. As the god of luck, I hold domain over that kind of thing.”

“This blessing is threefold. First, I bless you with immunity to misfortune. Second, I give you the ability to control who becomes the subject of the misfortune cast upon whomever looks on you. And thirdly, I greatly increase the misfortune you will cast upon those whom you deem fit to cast. You are doing well, my champion. Already, you have twelve Orbs. Soon, you may even have an Abomination. Continue doing God’s work, my child.” And with those final words, the water rippled and the mask vanished. Yeron stood up, having unconsciously knelt. He could feel the power flowing through him, not just around him. The Gibberings were champing at the bit to get at a place of such power, and he let them go.
